context_title: perrie you go your way meaning

entries.query: perrie you go your way meaning
entries.answer:
Perrie's "You Go Your Way" is a breakup song about two people agreeing to part ways — "you go your way, I'll go mine" — even though it hurts, but its true story is actually a happy one: it's about the moment her fiancé Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain refused to let her go and made their relationship official instead.

## The real story behind the song

The song was inspired by a conversation Perrie had with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (now her fiancé) when they first started dating in November 2016. At the time, Little Mix was about to go on tour with Ariana Grande for two and a half months, and Alex was busy with Arsenal, so Perrie didn't want to pressure him into waiting for her.[1][2]

She told him: "You go your way, I'll go mine and we'll just see where life takes us" — essentially offering to go their separate ways with no hard feelings, trusting that if they were meant to be together, it would happen anyway. Alex's response? "Urgh! Absolutely not, you're my girlfriend" — he rejected the whole idea and made the relationship official right there and then.[2][3]

Fast forward: they're now engaged, have a son named Axel, and the lyric "When we look back in five years time" references how five years after meeting in 2016, they had both welcomed their first child and gotten engaged.[2]

## What the song itself expresses

Taken at face value, the lyrics capture the bittersweet final moments of a relationship — driving home in tense silence, both knowing there's "a little space between us," and one person saying the dreaded "you go your way, I'll go mine". Key emotional beats:[4][5]

- "Okay, okay, okay, I'll be okay" — convincing yourself you'll survive the split
- The fear that once the car stops and they get home, they have to say the final goodbye
- The repeated "Go on, go on, go on and get over me" — pushing someone away even though it hurts[5][6]

Perrie herself summed up the philosophy behind it: "I truly believe if you love something, set it free. If it comes back, it's yours. If not it was never meant to be".[3]

## Broader interpretations

Perrie has said fans relate the song to their own situations — like leaving for university and "going their own way" from family and friends, or drifted-apart friendships — so she welcomes readings beyond the romantic one; for her it's ultimately about "taking that leap of faith".[7]

One side note: some fans have pointed out the track is based on a 2020 song of the same name by Joy Anonymous that Perrie's team appears to have acquired and reworked, though this doesn't change the personal narrative Perrie attached to it.[8]
